why: T51: the coordination-geometry gate counted only the lower-index endpoint of each stored bond, so it never fired for a metal above its partner. Records the population, the redundancy that hid it, and the before/after decode on a Pt_IV cloud.
code_change: molmetal/molmetal_lam/lam_chem/cfm_decoder_yuelbond.py _select_bonds(): bonds_at_metal now counts `a == metal_idx or b == metal_idx` instead of `a == metal_idx`.

population.note: candidate pairs come from torch.triu_indices(n, n, offset=1), so every stored pair has a < b

redundancy.claim: on the default valence table this gate never decides anything
redundancy.why_the_defect_was_invisible: an equal cap means the valence check refuses at the same point, so the geometry gate never produced the difference; Fe is the one table entry where the geometry is looser, and there the valence check binds first. The gate becomes the binding constraint only when a caller raises a cap past the geometry — valence_cap={78: 6} for Pt_IV.

synthetic_decode.cloud: 6 atoms: one Pt, five C on a pentagon of radius 1.9 A (Pt-C 1.90 A, C-C 2.23 A)
synthetic_decode.logits: BOND_SINGLE 10.0 on every Pt-C pair, NO_BOND 10.0 on every C-C pair

results.result: the 5th Pt bond is refused; the one-end count is blind

results.note: the valence cap refuses the 5th before the geometry gate is reached

results.result: the two counts agree on the 84.5% majority case

counts_both_ends.claim: a metal at the higher index is counted

pt_iv_cap_holds.claim: with valence_cap={78:6}, the 5th Pt bond is refused by the geometry gate

default_bit_exact.measured: metal_index=0: one-end count == both-end count on every bond, so the gate cannot behave differently there; 4 bonds kept as before
default_bit_exact.scope_note: this is a count-equality argument on the majority case, not a byte comparison against the pre-change decode

regression_guard: the two Pt_IV tests FAIL when the one-end expression is restored (verified by temporarily reverting the line): 2 failed, 2 passed
